summary: Native GitHub objectives support authored rolling throughput windows and a final-ready merge-latency budget. A 24h window with a five-per-hour minimum requires 120 merges. Targeted p95 latency counts open and late-merged PRs bad at their deadline and exposes completed-merge p95 diagnostics.

replay.detail: Measurements read corrected committed GitHub projections. No authoritative history rewrite or replay is required.

schema.detail: The local GitHub plugin adds an idempotently installed derived PR creation-time index for horizon-bounded deadline candidates. No claim fields, registry digest, convergence corpus, row layout or storage version changes. Indexed ready proofs gain an in-memory draft/unknown distinction.

compatibility.detail: Older evaluators reject merged-count windows and targeted ready-to-merged budgets as unsupported rather than evaluating the previous one-hour or measured-only policy. Existing declarations retain their one-hour default and all-author default. The native author-login selector applies to both indicators.

downtime.detail: First opening an existing populated GitHub plugin builds the creation-time index once; duration has not been measured. No restart or activation is performed by this change.

manual.detail: Upgrade evaluators before publishing the new declaration forms. Author the cohort, served objective ID, throughput window, latency deadline and budget in the owning policy; no fleet policy is embedded or applied.

recovery.detail: Restore declarations accepted by the previous evaluator before rolling back. Source facts remain unchanged.
